bug_semantics: CWE-918 SSRF: an unauthenticated proxy caller could supply x-headroom-base-url and make Headroom issue the request to a caller-selected http(s) destination. The original catch-all route passed that value directly to handle_passthrough, which appended the inbound path, copied all inbound headers except Host (including Authorization), sent the request with httpx, and returned the upstream response. Later OpenAI and Azure/passthrough resolution paths preserved the same trust error. Without rejecting loopback, link-local, RFC1918, metadata, or other non-public addresses, a remotely exposed proxy could disclose internal-service responses and forward caller credentials to the chosen host.
flaw_origin: 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f is the smallest first-writer. It added the x-headroom-base-url catch-all override in headroom/proxy/server.py and immediately passed custom_base.rstrip('/') to handle_passthrough without destination validation. The later b17c6d81cc39676f322779dc2e5695cba28b8e65 extraction into headroom/providers/proxy_routes.py, 7d747306066de6ed9f2635b58860f7d85fdf6362 compatibility work, and c19347c31046bf25baf9b1a816c9bede5d3ee807 OpenAI resolver are lifecycle moves/extensions, not the BIC.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f` shows human author and committer `chopratejas <chopratejas@gmail.com>` and no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI attribution trailer. A later extraction commit has an AI trailer, but it is not the BIC and is excluded by protocol.
evidence: In the assigned full-history clone, `git log --all --reverse -S'x-headroom-base-url' -- headroom` starts at 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f; `git log -L 6574,6578:headroom/proxy/server.py 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f` shows that commit adding `custom_base = request.headers.get("x-headroom-base-url")` and immediately returning `proxy.handle_passthrough(request, custom_base.rstrip("/"))`. `git show 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f:headroom/proxy/server.py` at handle_passthrough shows URL construction from base_url plus caller path, copying request headers and removing only Host, `http_client.request(...)`, and returning response content/headers. Direct parent check `git grep -n -i 'x-headroom-base-url' 55d8fb63614f56fde11b871a9b1d088c43040946 -- headroom/proxy/server.py` exits 1 with no match, while `git diff 55d8fb63614f56fde11b871a9b1d088c43040946 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f -- headroom/proxy/server.py` shows the addition. The first tagged descendant is v0.3.7 (`git tag --contains 729cc... --sort=version:refname`); the BIC itself bumps the source version to 0.3.5. Commit 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 added upstream_guard and protected the direct catch-all/OpenAI paths and shipped in v0.36.1, but it was incomplete: `git show v0.36.3:headroom/providers/proxy_targets.py` still shows select_passthrough_base_url returning the caller's x-headroom-base-url unchanged whenever caller-supplied `api-key` is present. The closing commit is 3e3c409436792129259cfae3d95179a94321f9ce: `git diff 1617f839a197ed1f17ca2083fbd288ffa2af7820 3e3c409436792129259cfae3d95179a94321f9ce -- headroom/providers/proxy_routes.py headroom/providers/proxy_targets.py headroom/providers/registry.py headroom/proxy/upstream_guard.py` shows CVE-2026-77775 guards added to the missed resolver/routes, plus bounded fail-closed DNS resolution and async route checks. `git tag --contains 3e3c... --sort=version:refname` starts at v0.36.4; v0.36.3 is therefore the last tagged vulnerable release and v0.36.4 (tag commit 91186b40d886c78e4b126d15837a51bea0a871e3) the first fully fixed release. Finally, `git cat-file -p 729cc...` reproduces the BIC-only marker check and shows no AI attribution.
reasoning: The causal defect is trusting a network client's destination header at the proxy boundary. The direct unsafe override first appears atomically in 729cc, and its immediate parent has no such header or route branch. Later refactoring only relocates it, and later OpenAI/Azure routing broadens the same vulnerability. Although 1f96 introduced the first SSRF guard, the advisory-named passthrough selector remained exploitable through its `api-key` branch through v0.36.3, so 3e3 is the minimum closing fix and v0.36.4 is the fixed boundary. The only admissible AI evidence is the 729cc commit object; it identifies a human and carries no AI marker, so the result is NOT_AI regardless of AI attribution on a later refactor.
